title: Digit Mixing under Polynomial Maps
summary: Let $X=\sum_{n\geq1}ξ_n2^{-n} $ be a random number where we model the digits $ξ_n$ as independent Bernoulli random variables with possibly non-identical parameters $p_n=\mathbb{P}(ξ_n=1)$. For any polynomial $P\in\mathbb{R}[X]$ with degree $d\geq2$, we prove almost sure absolute normality of $P(X)$ under the condition $p_n(1-p_n)\geq (\log n)^{Γ(d)} n^{-(d-1)/d}$ for a suitable constant $Γ(d)$ depending only on the degree $d$.
